signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Network devices (routers, switches, access points) Database management systems Application servers and web servers IoT devices and embedded systems Security cameras and physical security systems Remote access systems (VPN, remote desktop) Cloud service accounts Administrative consoles and web interfaces Container orchestration platforms Monitoring and logging systems

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal typically involves: Scanning for known default credential combinations Testing authentication with vendor-documented default passwords Checking for unchanged default API keys and tokens Reviewing system documentation for initial setup credentials Automated vulnerability scanning for default credentials Penetration testing and credential audits Comparing against databases of known defaults (e.g., CIRT.net Default Passwords Database) The presence of this signal represents a critical security risk that should be addressed immediately, as default credentials are often the first vector attempted by attackers.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 - Security and Privacy Controls

signals.name: Secure Configuration Baseline Missing
signals.description: No defined secure configuration standards or baselines exist for systems and applications within the environment. This signal indicates that there are no documented, approved configuration templates or standards against which system configurations can be validated, leading to inconsistent security postures and inability to detect configuration drift.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Operating system configurations Application server configurations Database system settings Network device configurations Cloud infrastructure resources Container and Kubernetes configurations Mobile device configurations Security appliance settings SaaS application configurations

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal typically involves: Reviewing for documented configuration baseline policies Checking for existence of approved configuration templates Examining configuration management tools and repositories Validating whether baseline compliance scanning is performed Assessing whether gold images or approved AMIs/images exist Reviewing for configuration standards documentation The presence of this signal indicates that configuration baseline standards should be developed and implemented.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 - Security and Privacy Controls

signals.name: Change Management Missing
signals.description: No formal process for requesting, approving, testing, and documenting system changes exists or is being followed. This signal indicates that configuration and system modifications may occur without proper oversight, documentation, or validation, leading to unauthorized changes, configuration drift, or unintended service disruptions.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Production system configuration changes Infrastructure modifications Application deployments and updates Network configuration changes Security policy modifications Cloud resource provisioning and changes Database schema and configuration changes Emergency or break-fix changes

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal typically involves: Reviewing for documented change management policies and procedures Checking for change request ticketing systems Validating approval workflows and audit trails Examining version control usage for infrastructure-as-code Assessing configuration drift between documented and actual state Reviewing deployment pipeline controls and approval gates The presence of this signal indicates that change management practices should be established or strengthened.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 - Security and Privacy Controls

signals.name: System Hardening Missing
signals.description: Systems are not configured according to security hardening baselines; default or insecure configurations remain in place. This signal indicates that systems may be running with vendor defaults, unnecessary services enabled, or without security hardening measures applied, increasing the attack surface and potential for compromise.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Server operating systems (Linux, Windows, Unix) Network devices (routers, switches, firewalls) Database management systems Web servers and application servers Cloud virtual machines and instances Container images and runtime environments IoT and embedded devices Mobile device management configurations

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal typically involves: Comparing current configurations against hardening benchmarks (CIS, DISA STIGs) Scanning for known insecure default settings Identifying unnecessary services and features enabled Checking for missing security-relevant configurations Validating against organization-specific baseline standards The presence of this signal indicates that a review of system hardening practices is warranted.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 - Security and Privacy Controls

signals.name: Certificate Management Missing
signals.description: No process for managing digital certificates including issuance, renewal, and revocation. This signal indicates the absence of formalized certificate lifecycle management practices, which can lead to expired certificates causing service outages, use of untrusted or self-signed certificates in production, inability to revoke compromised certificates, and lack of visibility into certificate inventory across the organization.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Web servers and APIs using TLS/SSL Internal PKI infrastructure Code signing certificates Client authentication certificates Email encryption certificates (S/MIME) VPN and network device certificates Container registry authentication Service mesh mutual TLS configurations IoT device certificates Mobile device management (MDM) certificates

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal typically involves: Scanning for certificates across infrastructure Checking certificate expiration dates Identifying self-signed certificates in production Reviewing certificate issuance and renewal processes Analyzing certificate chain validation Checking for certificate revocation list (CRL) or OCSP configurations Reviewing automation for certificate deployment Examining certificate monitoring and alerting systems Assessing certificate inventory and tracking mechanisms Common certificate management requirements: Maintain inventory of all certificates and their locations Monitor certificates for expiration (typically 30-90 day warnings) Automate certificate renewal where possible (e.g., Let's Encrypt, ACME) Use trusted certificate authorities for production syste

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 - Security and Privacy Controls

signals.name: Encryption at Rest Missing
signals.description: Sensitive data is not encrypted when stored in databases, file systems, or storage media. This signal indicates that data at rest lacks cryptographic protection, potentially exposing confidential information to unauthorized access through physical media theft, improper disposal, or unauthorized system access.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Databases storing sensitive or regulated data File systems containing confidential information Cloud storage services (S3, Azure Blob, GCS, etc.) Backup and archive systems Mobile devices and laptops Removable media (USB drives, external hard drives) Virtual machine disk images Container persistent volumes

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal typically involves: Scanning database configurations for encryption settings Examining storage service encryption parameters Reviewing file system encryption status Checking cloud resource encryption configurations Analyzing backup and archive encryption settings Verifying disk encryption on endpoints and servers The presence of this signal indicates a condition where sensitive data may be vulnerable to unauthorized access through physical or logical means when stored.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 - Security and Privacy Controls

signals.name: Encryption in Transit Missing
signals.description: Data is transmitted over networks without encryption (e.g., HTTP instead of HTTPS, unencrypted database connections). This signal indicates that data in transit lacks cryptographic protection, potentially exposing confidential information to interception, eavesdropping, or man-in-the-middle attacks during transmission across networks.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Web applications and APIs Database connections (client-to-server) Microservice communication Message queues and pub/sub systems Email transmission (SMTP) File transfer protocols (FTP, rsync) Remote access protocols (SSH, RDP) Mobile app backend communication Third-party API integrations

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal typically involves: Network traffic analysis for unencrypted protocols Scanning application configurations for HTTP vs HTTPS endpoints Examining database connection strings for SSL/TLS parameters Reviewing API client configurations Analyzing service mesh or ingress controller settings Checking email server configurations for TLS support Monitoring certificate usage across services The presence of this signal indicates a condition where data may be vulnerable to interception or tampering during network transmission.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 - Security and Privacy Controls

signals.name: Cryptographic Key Management Missing
signals.description: No documented process for generating, storing, rotating, or revoking cryptographic keys. This signal indicates the absence of formalized key management practices, which can lead to weak key generation, insecure key storage, failure to rotate keys, inability to revoke compromised keys, and overall compromise of cryptographic systems.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations using encryption for data protection Systems implementing cryptographic controls Key management systems (KMS) and HSM deployments Certificate authorities and PKI infrastructure API key and token management systems Cloud encryption services (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS) Database encryption implementations Application-level encryption systems

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal typically involves: Reviewing organizational documentation for key management policies Examining key storage mechanisms and access controls Checking for automated key rotation configurations Analyzing key lifecycle management procedures Verifying existence of key backup and recovery processes Reviewing audit logs for key access and operations Assessing separation of duties in key management Checking for key versioning and tracking mechanisms The presence of this signal indicates a systemic gap in cryptographic key management practices that may undermine the effectiveness of encryption controls.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 - Security and Privacy Controls

signals.name: Weak Cryptographic Algorithms Used
signals.description: Deprecated or cryptographically weak algorithms are in use (e.g., MD5, SHA-1, DES, RC4). This signal indicates that systems are using cryptographic algorithms that have known vulnerabilities, have been deprecated by standards bodies, or provide insufficient security for modern threat environments. Use of weak algorithms can enable attacks such as collision attacks, brute force decryption, or cryptanalysis.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Encryption implementations in applications Hash functions for password storage or integrity checking TLS/SSL configurations for web servers and APIs Digital signature implementations VPN and network encryption protocols Database encryption configurations Code signing and software distribution Blockchain and cryptocurrency implementations

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal typically involves: Static code analysis for deprecated cryptographic API usage TLS/SSL configuration scanning for weak protocols and cipher suites Reviewing cryptographic library configurations Analyzing certificate signature algorithms Checking password hashing implementations Scanning for legacy encryption protocols in network traffic Reviewing infrastructure-as-code for weak algorithm specifications Examining third-party dependencies for outdated crypto libraries Recommended strong alternatives: **Hash Functions**: SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA-3, BLAKE2 **Symmetric Encryption**: AES-256, ChaCha20 **Asymmetric Encryption**: RSA >= 2048 bits, ECDSA (P-256 or higher), Ed25519 **TLS/SSL Protocols**: TLS 1.2 (minimum), TLS 1.3 (preferred) **Key Derivation**: Argon

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 - Security and Privacy Controls

signals.name: Data Classification Missing
signals.description: No scheme for classifying data by sensitivity level (e.g., public, internal, confidential, restricted). Organizations lack a structured approach to categorizing data based on its sensitivity, value, and criticality. This signal indicates that data is not systematically labeled or classified according to its confidentiality, integrity, and availability requirements.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Document management systems Database systems and data warehouses Cloud storage platforms File sharing and collaboration tools Data processing pipelines API endpoints handling various data types Information security policies and procedures

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal typically involves: Reviewing data governance policies for classification requirements Scanning data stores for classification metadata or labels Checking file systems for classification tags or naming conventions Examining database schemas for sensitivity indicators Interviewing data owners about classification practices The presence of this signal indicates a foundational data governance gap that may affect an organization's ability to implement appropriate security controls, access restrictions, and compliance measures.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 - Security and Privacy Controls

signals.name: Secure Data Disposal Missing
signals.description: No process for securely disposing of data when no longer needed (secure deletion, media destruction). Organizations lack procedures and mechanisms to permanently and irrecoverably destroy data when it reaches the end of its retention period or is no longer required. This signal indicates data may remain accessible on storage media, backups, or decommissioned systems without proper sanitization or destruction.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Data deletion and purging processes Media sanitization and destruction programs Decommissioning of storage systems and servers Hard drive and backup tape disposal Cloud storage lifecycle management Database record deletion procedures Device disposal and recycling programs

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal typically involves: Reviewing disposal and sanitization policies Examining media destruction logs and certificates Checking database deletion procedures (soft vs. hard delete) Analyzing decommissioning processes for IT assets Assessing cloud storage lifecycle configurations Reviewing backup retention and deletion practices Inspecting physical security for media disposal The absence of secure disposal processes creates data breach risks from improperly decommissioned equipment, increases storage costs, complicates compliance with data protection regulations, and may expose sensitive data through surplus equipment sales or donations. Secure disposal should align with recognized standards such as NIST SP 800-88 (Guidelines for Media Sanitization), DoD 5220.22-M, or eq

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 - Security and Privacy Controls

signals.name: Data Inventory Missing
signals.description: No inventory documenting what sensitive data exists and where it is stored. Organizations lack a comprehensive record or catalog of sensitive data assets across their environment. This signal indicates an absence of systematic documentation identifying data types, locations, systems, data flows, and responsible parties for sensitive information.

signals.description: A secret was committed to version control and remains in the repository's commit history, even if later removed from the current codebase. signals.name: Secret Rotation Missing
signals.description: Secrets, credentials, API keys, and passwords are not regularly rotated according to a defined schedule. This signal indicates that sensitive authentication material remains static over extended periods, increasing the risk of unauthorized access if credentials are compromised. Regular rotation limits the window of opportunity for attackers using stolen or leaked credentials.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: API keys and tokens (cloud providers, SaaS platforms, third-party services) Database passwords and connection strings Service account credentials Application secrets and encryption keys OAuth client secrets and refresh tokens SSH keys and TLS/SSL certificates Webhook signing secrets Integration credentials (CI/CD, monitoring, logging) Administrative and privileged account passwords

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal typically involves: Monitoring credential creation and last-modified timestamps Tracking time elapsed since last rotation Auditing rotation policies and schedules in identity management systems Analyzing credential metadata from cloud provider APIs Reviewing certificate and key expiration dates Examining password age in directory services The presence of this signal indicates a potential gap in credential lifecycle management practices. Many frameworks require rotation at specific intervals (e.g., 90 days for PCI DSS), while best practices suggest rotation based on risk assessment and the sensitivity of protected resources.

signals.name: Plaintext Secret in Source Code
signals.description: A secret value (such as an API key, password, token, or private key) is present in plaintext within source code or version-controlled files. This signal indicates that sensitive credential material is embedded directly in code artifacts rather than being externalized to secure storage or runtime injection mechanisms.
signals.applicability: Applicable to any source code repository, version control system, or code artifact where secrets may be inadvertently or intentionally committed. Includes application code, configuration files, infrastructure-as-code templates, scripts, and notebooks.

metadata.detection_notes: Commonly detected through pattern matching, entropy analysis, or known secret formats in source files. Detection tools may scan commit history to identify secrets introduced at any point in the repository lifecycle.

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review Business Associate Agreements to verify they include provisions requiring subcontractors to comply with the same safeguards. Examine contract templates and executed agreements for subcontractor flow-down clauses. Assess whether business associates have processes to ensure subcontractors execute appropriate agreements before handling ePHI.

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review physical access control procedures including badge systems, visitor logs, and escort requirements. Verify that access is granted based on role-based authorization and that validation mechanisms are in place. Check for documented visitor management procedures, sign-in/sign-out logs, and controls for accessing areas with development or testing systems.

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review policies and procedures for emergency facility access controls. Verify that documented procedures exist for granting physical access during disaster recovery operations and emergency mode operations. Check for integration with the organization's disaster recovery and business continuity plans.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Physical Safeguards
NIST SP 800-66 Rev 2 - Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule

signals.name: No Facility Security Plan

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Examine facility security documentation for comprehensive policies addressing physical access controls, anti-tampering measures, and theft prevention. Review physical security assessments, perimeter security controls, surveillance systems, and alarm systems. Verify that procedures address all areas where ePHI is accessed, stored, or transmitted.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Physical Safeguards
NIST SP 800-66 Rev 2 - Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review maintenance logs and work order systems for documentation of security-related facility modifications. Verify that records exist for repairs or changes to locks, doors, walls, access control systems, surveillance equipment, and other physical security components. Check for procedures requiring documentation before and after security-related maintenance activities.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Physical Safeguards
NIST SP 800-66 Rev 2 - Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule

signals.name: No Media Disposal

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review media disposal and sanitization policies and procedures. Verify that documented processes exist for secure destruction or disposal of ePHI and storage media, including hard drives, backup tapes, CDs/DVDs, USB drives, and mobile devices. Check for procedures addressing physical destruction, degaussing, cryptographic erasure, or certified data destruction services with certificates of destruction.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Physical Safeguards
NIST SP 800-66 Rev 2 - Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule

signals.name: No Media Re-use Controls

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review procedures for sanitizing storage media before reallocation or repurposing. Verify that documented processes exist for securely removing ePHI from media intended for re-use, including formatting, wiping, or cryptographic erasure methods. Check for procedures addressing different media types and verification of successful data removal before media is reassigned or released.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Physical Safeguards

signals.name: No Workstation Security

Verify implementation of safeguards such as locking mechanisms, secure mounting, cable locks, proximity sensors, or placement in restricted access areas. Check for controls preventing unauthorized physical access to workstations, including laptop security, screen positioning, and automatic lock features when unattended.

Verify that documented procedures specify allowable functions for workstations accessing ePHI, proper usage protocols, and requirements for physical placement and surroundings. Check for policies addressing privacy screens, workstation positioning to prevent unauthorized viewing, and secure areas for workstations handling sensitive ePHI.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Physical Safeguards
NIST SP 800-66 Rev 2 - Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule

signals.name: No Individual Access Rights

metadata.detection_notes: Detect absence of access request mechanisms, denied access requests without valid grounds for denial, or systems that do not provide individuals the ability to inspect and obtain copies of their PHI in designated record sets.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Human resources and workforce management functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detect access requests pending beyond the 30-day timeframe without proper extension notification, or requests that exceed the maximum 60-day response time (30 days plus one 30-day extension). Monitor request tracking systems for overdue access requests.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No Accounting of Disclosures
signals.description: No accounting of disclosures provided when requested.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Human resources and workforce management functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detect absence of disclosure tracking mechanisms, incomplete accounting records, or failure to provide accounting within 60 days of request (with possible 30-day extension). Monitor for disclosure logs that do not capture required information (date, recipient, description, purpose).

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No Amendment Rights
signals.description: Individuals not permitted to request amendments to their PHI.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Human resources and workforce management functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detect absence of amendment request processes, denied amendment requests without valid grounds for denial (record not created by entity, record not in designated record set, record not available for inspection, or record is accurate and complete), or systems lacking amendment request functionality.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No Valid Authorization

signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: PHI is used or disclosed without obtaining required written authorization Authorizations are missing required core elements (description of PHI, purpose, expiration, etc.) Authorizations lack required statements (right to revoke, treatment/payment not conditioned, etc.) Authorizations are obtained through defective notices or forms Authorizations are used beyond their expiration date Compound authorizations are improperly combined Revoked authorizations are not honored

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No Complaint Process

signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Human resources and workforce management functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detect absence of documented complaint procedures, inaccessible complaint mechanisms, or missing complaint contact information in privacy notices. Verify that individuals have clear pathways to file complaints both internally and with HHS Office for Civil Rights.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No Confidential Communications
signals.description: No accommodation of requests for confidential communications.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: No process exists for individuals to request confidential communications Reasonable requests for alternative communication methods or locations are denied Healthcare providers improperly require explanations for confidential communication requests Health plans fail to accommodate requests when disclosure could endanger the individual Alternative addresses, phone numbers, or email addresses are not honored Systems are not configured to support confidential communication preferences Staff are not trained on confidential communication obligations Documentation of confidential communication requests and accommodations is inadequate

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No De-identification Standards
signals.description: No proper de-identification of health information using Expert Determination or Safe Harbor methods.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: De-identified data sets retain identifiers from the Safe Harbor list of 18 identifiers No expert determination has been obtained for de-identification methods Safe Harbor method is not properly applied with all required identifiers removed De-identification processes lack documentation or validation Re-identification risk assessments are not performed Limited data sets are created without proper data use agreements

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No Marketing Authorization
signals.description: PHI used for marketing without required authorization or disclosure of financial remuneration.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: Marketing communications are sent without obtaining required authorization Authorizations for marketing fail to disclose financial remuneration from third parties Treatment or health plan communications are mischaracterized to avoid marketing authorization requirements Refill reminders or health-related product recommendations contain marketing elements without authorization Face-to-face exception or nominal gift exception is improperly applied Financial incentives for marketing are not disclosed in authorizations

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No Minimum Necessary Standard
signals.description: No reasonable efforts to limit PHI to minimum necessary for the intended purpose.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: PHI disclosures include more information than necessary for the stated purpose Policies and procedures for minimum necessary determinations are absent or inadequate System configurations allow access to entire medical records when limited access would suffice Requests for PHI do not specify the minimum amount needed Regular reviews of minimum necessary practices are not conducted

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No Mitigation of Harmful Effects
signals.description: No mitigation of known harmful effects of privacy violations.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Human resources and workforce management functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detect known privacy violations without documented mitigation efforts, failure to address harmful effects of unauthorized disclosures, or absence of remediation actions following privacy incidents. Monitor incident response procedures for mitigation steps taken to reduce harm to affected individuals.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: Incomplete Notice Content
signals.description: Notice of Privacy Practices does not contain all required elements.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: Notice lacks required header stating "THIS NOTICE DESCRIBES HOW MEDICAL INFORMATION ABOUT YOU MAY BE USED AND DISCLOSED..." Description of uses and disclosures is incomplete or inaccurate Individual rights section omits required rights (access, amendment, accounting, restrictions, confidential communications) Covered entity duties are not properly described Complaint procedures and contact information are missing or incomplete Effective date is absent or incorrect Required statements about marketing, fundraising, or sale of PHI are missing Notice does not describe state law protections that are more stringent than HIPAA

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No Notice Provision to Individuals
signals.description: Notice not provided at first service delivery, upon request, or as otherwise required.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: Notice is not provided at first service delivery to new patients or plan enrollees Notice is not provided promptly after emergency treatment Notice is not made available electronically when individuals access PHI through electronic means Good faith effort to obtain written acknowledgment is not documented Notice is not provided within required timeframes when material changes occur Notice is not posted in clear and prominent locations in facilities Notice is not available upon request Health plans fail to provide notice at enrollment or within 60 days of material revision

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No Privacy Contact Person
signals.description: No designated contact person/office for receiving complaints and providing information.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Human resources and workforce management functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detect absence of designated contact information in privacy notices, websites, or patient-facing materials. Verify that contact person/office information is current and accessible to individuals seeking to file complaints or obtain privacy information.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No Notice of Privacy Practices
signals.description: No Notice of Privacy Practices provided to individuals.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: Covered entities fail to develop or maintain a Notice of Privacy Practices Notice is not available for distribution to individuals Notice has not been updated to reflect material changes in privacy practices Electronic notice availability requirements are not met for entities with web presence Notice is not available in the language or format needed by the individual population served Documentation of notice provision is not maintained

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No Designated Privacy Official
signals.description: No designated privacy official responsible for privacy policies and procedures.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Human resources and workforce management functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detect absence of documented privacy official designation, vacancy in the privacy official role, or organizational documentation lacking privacy officer identification. Review organizational charts, policy documents, and privacy notices for privacy official designation.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No Privacy Training
signals.description: No training provided to workforce members on privacy policies and procedures.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Human resources and workforce management functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detect workforce members without documented privacy training, new hires not trained within reasonable timeframes, or absence of training updates following material policy changes. Monitor training completion records, onboarding processes, and retraining after policy updates.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No Psychotherapy Notes Protection
signals.description: Psychotherapy notes used or disclosed without required authorization.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: Psychotherapy notes are disclosed without specific authorization separate from other PHI authorizations Psychotherapy notes are improperly commingled with general medical records Notes that do not meet the definition of psychotherapy notes are incorrectly segregated Psychotherapy notes are used for purposes beyond the narrow exceptions (originator's treatment use, training, legal defense, oversight) Providers fail to maintain separate storage and access controls for psychotherapy notes

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No Rights to Request Restrictions
signals.description: Individuals not permitted to request restrictions on uses and disclosures of their PHI.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: Individuals are prevented from making restriction requests No process exists for receiving and tracking restriction requests Required restrictions (out-of-pocket payment in full) are not honored Agreed-upon restrictions are not implemented in systems or workflows Restrictions are not properly documented Terminated restrictions are not properly communicated to affected parties Emergency circumstances exception to restrictions is improperly applied Restriction request denials are not properly documented or communicated

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No Retaliation Protection
signals.description: Intimidation or retaliation against individuals exercising their privacy rights.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Human resources and workforce management functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detect adverse actions taken against individuals who exercised privacy rights, filed complaints, or participated in investigations. Monitor for patterns of denials of service, increased costs, or other retaliatory measures following privacy-related activities. Review complaints alleging intimidation or retaliation.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No Administrative/Technical/Physical Safeguards
signals.description: No appropriate administrative, technical, and physical safeguards to protect PHI.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Human resources and workforce management functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detect absence of documented safeguards, inadequate access controls, lack of physical security measures, or insufficient technical protections for PHI. Evaluate administrative policies, technical security controls (encryption, authentication, audit logs), and physical security measures (locked files, secure facilities, visitor controls).

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No PHI Sale Prohibition
signals.description: PHI disclosed for remuneration without proper authorization.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: PHI is disclosed in exchange for direct or indirect remuneration without authorization Authorization for sale of PHI does not explicitly state that remuneration is involved Exceptions for public health purposes, research, treatment/payment, business associate services, or individual-requested disclosures are improperly applied Financial arrangements involving PHI disclosure are not properly documented Data brokers or third parties receive PHI in exchange for payment without proper authorization Reasonable cost-based fees are exceeded, constituting remuneration

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No Sanctions for Non-Compliance
signals.description: No sanctions applied against workforce members for privacy violations.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Human resources and workforce management functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detect absence of documented sanction policies, failure to apply sanctions for confirmed privacy violations, or lack of enforcement of privacy policies. Review incident response records, disciplinary actions, and workforce accountability measures for privacy non-compliance.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No Treatment/Payment/Operations Limits
signals.description: Uses and disclosures for treatment, payment, or health care operations exceed permitted scope.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: PHI is disclosed for treatment beyond what is necessary for coordinating care Payment-related disclosures exceed billing and reimbursement purposes Health care operations uses go beyond permitted activities (quality assessment, training, accreditation, etc.) TPO purposes are broadly interpreted to justify inappropriate disclosures Notice of Privacy Practices does not adequately describe TPO uses and disclosures

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No Limits on Uses and Disclosures
signals.canonical_name: No Limits on Uses and Disclosures
signals.description: No limits on uses and disclosures of PHI; disclosures made beyond permitted or required purposes.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: PHI is used or disclosed for purposes not explicitly permitted by HIPAA Disclosures are made without proper authorization or legal basis PHI is shared beyond the scope of permitted purposes Monitoring reveals uses and disclosures that exceed regulatory permissions

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No Waiver Prohibition
signals.description: Individuals required to waive rights as condition of treatment, payment, or benefits.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Human resources and workforce management functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detect forms, agreements, or policies requiring waiver of access rights (164.524) or accounting of disclosures rights (164.528) as a condition of receiving treatment, payment, plan enrollment, or benefits eligibility. Review consent forms, enrollment documents, and service agreements for prohibited waiver language.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

signals.name: No Audit Controls
signals.description: No hardware, software, or procedural mechanisms to record and examine activity in systems containing ePHI.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Electronic health record (EHR) systems Health information exchanges (HIEs) Patient portals and healthcare applications Database systems containing ePHI Network infrastructure transmitting ePHI Cloud services hosting healthcare data

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review system logging configurations and audit trail capabilities. Verify that systems capture user access, modifications, deletions, and other activities involving ePHI. Check for centralized log management, log retention policies, and regular audit log reviews. Identify systems with disabled logging or insufficient audit trail detail.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Technical Safeguards
NIST SP 800-66 Rev 2 - Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule

signals.name: No Person or Entity Authentication
signals.description: No procedures to verify that a person or entity seeking access to ePHI is the one claimed.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Electronic health record (EHR) systems Health information exchanges (HIEs) Patient portals and healthcare applications Database systems containing ePHI Network infrastructure transmitting ePHI Cloud services hosting healthcare data

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Evaluate authentication mechanisms including password policies, multi-factor authentication, biometric systems, and certificate-based authentication. Check for weak authentication methods such as simple passwords without complexity requirements, absence of account lockout policies, or systems that do not properly verify user credentials before granting access to ePHI.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Technical Safeguards
NIST SP 800-66 Rev 2 - Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule

signals.name: No Automatic Logoff
signals.description: No electronic procedures to terminate sessions after predetermined period of inactivity.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Electronic health record (EHR) systems Health information exchanges (HIEs) Patient portals and healthcare applications Database systems containing ePHI Network infrastructure transmitting ePHI Cloud services hosting healthcare data

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Test application and system session timeout settings to verify automatic logoff functionality. Check for configured idle timeout periods in web applications, terminal sessions, and database connections. Monitor for systems that allow indefinite session persistence or require manual logout only.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Technical Safeguards
NIST SP 800-66 Rev 2 - Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule

signals.name: No Emergency Access Procedure
signals.description: No procedures for obtaining necessary ePHI during an emergency.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Electronic health record (EHR) systems Health information exchanges (HIEs) Patient portals and healthcare applications Database systems containing ePHI Network infrastructure transmitting ePHI Cloud services hosting healthcare data

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review system documentation and incident response procedures to verify the existence of emergency access protocols. Check for documented procedures that allow authorized personnel to access ePHI during system failures, disasters, or other emergency situations. Verify that emergency access mechanisms are tested and that access is properly logged and audited.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Technical Safeguards
NIST SP 800-66 Rev 2 - Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule

signals.name: No Encryption and Decryption
signals.description: No mechanism to encrypt and decrypt ePHI.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Electronic health record (EHR) systems Health information exchanges (HIEs) Patient portals and healthcare applications Database systems containing ePHI Network infrastructure transmitting ePHI Cloud services hosting healthcare data

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Examine data storage configurations, database encryption settings, and file system encryption status. Check for unencrypted ePHI at rest on servers, workstations, portable devices, and backup media. Verify encryption standards and key management practices for systems that do implement encryption.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Technical Safeguards
NIST SP 800-66 Rev 2 - Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule

signals.name: No ePHI Integrity Mechanism
signals.description: No electronic mechanisms to corroborate that ePHI has not been altered or destroyed in an unauthorized manner.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Electronic health record (EHR) systems Health information exchanges (HIEs) Patient portals and healthcare applications Database systems containing ePHI Network infrastructure transmitting ePHI Cloud services hosting healthcare data

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Examine systems for integrity verification mechanisms such as digital signatures, hash functions, checksums, or blockchain technologies. Review change management processes and version control systems for ePHI. Check for file integrity monitoring tools and database audit trails that detect unauthorized modifications.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Technical Safeguards
NIST SP 800-66 Rev 2 - Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule

signals.name: No Transmission Encryption
signals.description: No mechanism to encrypt ePHI whenever deemed appropriate during transmission.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Electronic health record (EHR) systems Health information exchanges (HIEs) Patient portals and healthcare applications Database systems containing ePHI Network infrastructure transmitting ePHI Cloud services hosting healthcare data

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Analyze network traffic and communication channels for unencrypted ePHI transmission. Check for proper implementation of TLS/SSL for web applications, VPN usage for remote access, and encrypted protocols for file transfers (SFTP, FTPS). Verify that email containing ePHI uses encryption (S/MIME, PGP, or secure email gateways) and that API communications use HTTPS.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Technical Safeguards
NIST SP 800-66 Rev 2 - Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule

signals.name: No Transmission Integrity Controls
signals.description: No security measures to ensure electronically transmitted ePHI is not improperly modified without detection.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Electronic health record (EHR) systems Health information exchanges (HIEs) Patient portals and healthcare applications Database systems containing ePHI Network infrastructure transmitting ePHI Cloud services hosting healthcare data

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review network transmission protocols and security measures for ePHI transfers. Check for integrity verification mechanisms such as message authentication codes (MACs), digital signatures, or secure protocols (TLS/SSL) that include integrity checking. Verify that file transfers, API communications, and messaging systems implement tamper detection.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Technical Safeguards
NIST SP 800-66 Rev 2 - Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule

signals.name: No Unique User Identification
signals.description: No unique name and/or number assigned for identifying and tracking user identity.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Electronic health record (EHR) systems Health information exchanges (HIEs) Patient portals and healthcare applications Database systems containing ePHI Network infrastructure transmitting ePHI Cloud services hosting healthcare data

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Examine user account configurations, authentication systems, and access logs to verify that each user has been assigned a unique identifier. Look for shared accounts, generic usernames (e.g., "admin", "user"), or systems that allow multiple users to authenticate with the same credentials.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Technical Safeguards
NIST SP 800-66 Rev 2 - Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule

signals.name: Access Logging Not Implemented
signals.description: Logging of user access events and authentication attempts is not implemented for systems containing protected health information (PHI) or other sensitive data. This signal indicates the absence of audit logs that capture user login events, logout events, failed authentication attempts, access to sensitive resources, and privilege escalation activities. Access logging is essential for security monitoring, incident investigation, compliance verification, and detecting unauthorized access attempts.
signals.applicability: Healthcare organizations subject to HIPAA Business associates handling PHI Organizations pursuing HITRUST certification Systems processing sensitive health information Web applications and patient portals Electronic health record (EHR) systems Database management systems Cloud infrastructure and services Identity and access management (IAM) systems Remote access systems (VPN, remote desktop)

signals.canonical_name: No Identification of Legal and Regulatory Requirements
signals.description: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements relevant to security are not identified and documented.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization has not identified, documented, and maintained awareness of applicable legal, statutory, regulatory, and contractual requirements related to information security and the protection of information assets.

metadata.detection_notes: Review compliance register or requirements documentation, verify legal and regulatory monitoring processes, check for contractual obligation tracking, assess requirements communication to relevant personnel, examine compliance assessment and gap analysis processes.

signals.name: No Management Security Responsibilities
signals.description: Management does not require personnel to apply information security in accordance with established policies and procedures.
signals.applicability: Applies when management does not actively enforce security policies, lacks accountability mechanisms for security compliance, or fails to demonstrate leadership in information security practices.

metadata.detection_notes: Review management communications regarding security expectations, assess security enforcement mechanisms, interview personnel about management support for security, evaluate consequences for security policy violations, verify management participation in security reviews.

signals.name: No Privacy and Protection of PII
signals.canonical_name: No Privacy and Protection of PII
signals.description: Privacy and protection of personally identifiable information is not ensured as required.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization does not identify and meet privacy and PII protection requirements applicable to the organization, including compliance with privacy laws, data subject rights, consent management, and cross-border data transfer controls.

metadata.detection_notes: Review privacy policies and procedures, verify PII inventory and data mapping, check consent management processes, assess data subject rights procedures, examine data protection impact assessments, verify cross-border transfer mechanisms, review privacy training and awareness.

signals.name: No Information Security in Project Management
signals.canonical_name: No Information Security in Project Management
signals.description: Information security is not integrated into project management regardless of project type.
signals.applicability: Applies when organizations run projects without incorporating security requirements, security reviews, or security acceptance criteria in project planning, execution, and delivery phases.

metadata.detection_notes: Review project templates and methodologies for security integration, assess project charters for security requirements, verify security checkpoints in project gates, check for security acceptance criteria in project deliverables.

signals.name: No Protection of Records
signals.description: Records are not protected from loss, destruction, falsification, and unauthorized access.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization does not adequately protect important records from loss, destruction, falsification, unauthorized access, and unauthorized release in accordance with legal, regulatory, contractual, and business requirements.

metadata.detection_notes: Review records management policies and procedures, verify records classification and retention schedules, check access controls for records systems, assess backup and recovery for records, examine disposal procedures for records, verify compliance with retention requirements.

signals.name: No Information Security Policies
signals.description: Organization lacks documented information security policies approved by management, published, and communicated to relevant parties.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization does not have formally documented, management-approved information security policies that are published and communicated to personnel and relevant external parties.

metadata.detection_notes: Review documentation repositories for security policy documents, verify management approval signatures, check communication records to personnel, assess policy review and update processes.

signals.name: No Information Security Roles and Responsibilities
signals.canonical_name: No Information Security Roles and Responsibilities
signals.description: Information security roles and responsibilities are not defined and allocated according to organizational needs.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization has not formally defined and documented security roles, responsibilities are not clearly allocated, or personnel are unclear about their information security obligations.

metadata.detection_notes: Review organizational charts and role descriptions for security responsibilities, interview personnel about their security obligations, assess RACI matrices for security functions, verify documentation of security role assignments.

signals.name: No Information Security in Supplier Agreements
signals.canonical_name: No Information Security in Supplier Agreements
signals.description: Supplier agreements do not establish relevant information security requirements based on supply relationship type.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization has supplier agreements that lack adequate information security requirements, terms, and conditions appropriate to the type of supplier relationship and the information assets that may be accessed, processed, stored, communicated, or provided.

metadata.detection_notes: Review supplier contracts and agreements for information security clauses, verify security requirements are defined based on supplier access levels, check for security obligations and SLA definitions, assess incident response and breach notification terms.

signals.name: No Supplier Service Monitoring and Review
signals.canonical_name: No Supplier Service Monitoring and Review
signals.description: Supplier service delivery is not regularly monitored, reviewed, and audited for security compliance.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization does not have established processes to regularly monitor, review, and audit supplier service levels and information security practices to ensure ongoing compliance with security requirements and contractual obligations.

metadata.detection_notes: Review supplier performance monitoring procedures, verify existence of regular security reviews, check audit schedules and findings, assess change management processes for supplier services, examine incident tracking and resolution with suppliers.

signals.name: No Supplier Security Management
signals.description: Processes for managing security risks associated with supplier access to organizational assets are not defined.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization lacks processes to identify, assess, and mitigate security risks in supplier relationships, including vendor due diligence, security requirements in contracts, and ongoing monitoring of supplier security posture.

metadata.detection_notes: Review supplier security assessment processes, verify security requirements in contracts and SLAs, assess supplier risk classifications, check for vendor security questionnaires, evaluate ongoing supplier monitoring, verify incident notification requirements.

signals.name: No ICT Supply Chain Security Management
signals.canonical_name: No ICT Supply Chain Security Management
signals.description: Processes for managing ICT supply chain security risks are not defined and implemented.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization lacks defined processes and controls to manage information security risks associated with ICT products and services throughout the supply chain lifecycle, including supplier selection, onboarding, and ongoing management.

metadata.detection_notes: Assess whether supply chain security policies exist, verify supplier security assessment procedures, check for ICT product and service security evaluation processes, review supplier risk management documentation, examine controls for supply chain transparency and integrity.

signals.name: No Threat Intelligence Program
signals.description: Organization does not collect and analyze threat intelligence to inform security decisions and controls.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization lacks a systematic approach to gathering, analyzing, and applying threat intelligence from internal and external sources to inform risk assessments and security control decisions.

metadata.detection_notes: Review threat intelligence sources and subscriptions, assess threat analysis processes, verify integration of threat intelligence into risk assessments, check for threat hunting activities, evaluate security control adjustments based on threat landscape changes.

signals.name: No Information Transfer Controls
signals.description: Rules, procedures, and agreements for secure information transfer are not in place.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization lacks controls for transferring information between the organization and external parties, including procedures for electronic transmission, physical transport, and verbal communication of sensitive information.

metadata.detection_notes: Review information transfer policies and procedures, assess encryption requirements for data in transit, verify secure file transfer mechanisms, check agreements with external parties for security requirements, evaluate controls for physical media transport.

signals.name: No Security Violation Disciplinary Process
signals.description: No formal disciplinary process exists for personnel who commit information security policy violations.
signals.applicability: HR policies, security violation handling, policy enforcement

metadata.detection_notes: Review HR policies, disciplinary procedures, and incident response documentation for defined processes addressing information security policy violations.

signals.name: No Security Terms in Employment Contracts
signals.canonical_name: No Security Terms in Employment Contracts
signals.description: Employment contracts do not state personnel and organization responsibilities for information security.
signals.applicability: Employment contracts, contractor agreements, security acknowledgments

metadata.detection_notes: Review employment contract templates, contractor agreements, and onboarding documentation for inclusion of information security responsibilities and obligations.

signals.name: No Security Event Reporting Mechanism
signals.description: Mechanism for personnel to report observed or suspected security events is not provided.
signals.applicability: Incident reporting channels, security awareness, reporting procedures

metadata.detection_notes: Review incident reporting procedures, available reporting channels, and personnel awareness of how to report security events. Verify accessibility and effectiveness of reporting mechanisms.

signals.name: No Confidentiality Agreements
signals.description: Confidentiality or NDA requirements are not identified, documented, and regularly reviewed.
signals.applicability: Employment, third parties, sensitive information access

metadata.detection_notes: Review employment contracts, third-party agreements, and vendor contracts for presence of confidentiality clauses and NDAs. Verify regular review processes exist.

signals.name: No Remote Working Security Controls
signals.description: Security measures for remote working are not implemented to protect information accessed or processed.
signals.applicability: Remote work policies, home office security, mobile device use

metadata.detection_notes: Review remote work policies, endpoint security configurations, VPN usage, and home office security requirements to identify gaps in remote working protections.

signals.name: No Personnel Screening
signals.description: Background verification checks on candidates are not carried out prior to joining and on an ongoing basis.
signals.applicability: HR processes, contractor onboarding, privileged access roles

metadata.detection_notes: Review HR onboarding procedures, background check policies, and verification records for candidates and existing personnel with privileged access.

signals.name: No Security Awareness Training
signals.description: Personnel do not receive appropriate security awareness education, training, and updates.
signals.applicability: All personnel, contractors, regular training programs

metadata.detection_notes: Review training records, security awareness program documentation, and onboarding materials to verify presence and currency of security education initiatives.

signals.name: No Post-Employment Security Process
signals.description: Security responsibilities that remain valid after termination or change are not defined and enforced.
signals.applicability: Offboarding, role changes, confidentiality obligations

metadata.detection_notes: Review offboarding procedures, access revocation processes, and post-employment obligation documentation to verify comprehensive security controls during employment transitions.

signals.name: No Cabling Security
signals.description: Cables carrying power and data are not protected from interception, interference, or damage.
signals.applicability: Organizations with power and data cabling infrastructure requiring protection from unauthorized access, tampering, and physical damage

metadata.detection_notes: Assess cabling infrastructure for protection against interception (shielding, encryption), interference (separation from power), and damage (conduit, labeling, access control). Exposed cables, poor cable management, or unprotected cable runs indicate this deficiency.

signals.name: No Clear Desk and Clear Screen Policy
signals.canonical_name: No Clear Desk and Clear Screen Policy
signals.description: Clear desk and clear screen rules for papers and removable storage media are not defined and enforced.
signals.applicability: Organizations where personnel handle sensitive information in physical form or on computer screens that could be viewed by unauthorized persons

metadata.detection_notes: Review policies for clear desk (securing physical documents when unattended) and clear screen (locking workstations when away). Absence of documented policies, lack of enforcement, or observation of unattended sensitive materials indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Physical Entry Controls
signals.description: Secure areas are not protected by appropriate entry controls and access points.
signals.applicability: Organizations with secure areas requiring controlled access to protect sensitive information and assets

metadata.detection_notes: Examine access control mechanisms at entry points to secure areas. Look for absence of badge readers, locks, security personnel, visitor management systems, or access logs. Unrestricted entry to sensitive areas indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Equipment Maintenance Controls
signals.description: Equipment is not maintained correctly to ensure availability and integrity.
signals.applicability: Organizations with information processing equipment requiring regular maintenance to ensure continued operation and data integrity

metadata.detection_notes: Review equipment maintenance schedules, service records, vendor qualifications, and data protection during maintenance. Absence of maintenance schedules, unqualified service providers, or lack of data protection procedures indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Equipment Siting and Protection
signals.description: Equipment is not sited securely and protected against environmental threats and unauthorized access.
signals.applicability: Organizations with information processing equipment that requires protection from environmental hazards and unauthorized access or damage

metadata.detection_notes: Assess equipment placement considering environmental risks (water, heat, dust), physical access risks, and protection measures (secure mounting, cable locks, environmental controls). Equipment in vulnerable locations or lacking protective measures indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Facility Security Measures
signals.description: Physical security for offices, rooms, and facilities is not designed and implemented.
signals.applicability: Organizations with offices, rooms, and facilities that require physical security measures to protect personnel and assets

metadata.detection_notes: Review facility security measures including locks, alarms, reinforced doors/windows, and security design. Absence of documented security design or implementation of protective measures for offices and facilities indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Storage Media Controls
signals.description: Storage media is not managed through its lifecycle according to classification and handling requirements.
signals.applicability: Organizations using storage media (physical and removable) that requires lifecycle management from acquisition through disposal

metadata.detection_notes: Review media management procedures including inventory, classification, storage, transportation, and disposal. Absence of documented procedures, untracked media, improper storage, or lack of secure disposal processes indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Off-Site Asset Security
signals.description: Off-site assets are not protected considering different risks of working outside organization premises.
signals.applicability: Organizations with assets located outside organizational premises including remote work, mobile computing, and assets at third-party locations

metadata.detection_notes: Review security measures for remote work, mobile devices, portable equipment, and assets at vendor or customer sites. Absence of policies for off-site work, lack of encryption, missing device tracking, or inadequate physical security controls indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Secure Area Working Rules
signals.description: Security measures for working in secure areas are not designed and implemented.
signals.applicability: Organizations with designated secure areas where specific security protocols must be followed during work activities

metadata.detection_notes: Review policies and procedures for working in secure areas including visitor escort requirements, photography restrictions, unattended work rules, and secure area awareness. Absence of documented rules or evidence of enforcement indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Secure Disposal or Re-use Procedures
signals.canonical_name: No Secure Disposal or Re-use Procedures
signals.description: Items containing storage media are not verified to ensure sensitive data is removed before disposal.
signals.applicability: Organizations disposing of or re-using equipment and media that may contain sensitive information

metadata.detection_notes: Review disposal and re-use procedures for equipment and media including data sanitization, physical destruction, verification processes, and certificates of destruction. Absence of documented procedures, unverified disposal, or lack of sanitization indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Physical Security Monitoring
signals.description: Premises are not continuously monitored for unauthorized physical access.
signals.applicability: Organizations requiring continuous monitoring of physical premises to detect and respond to unauthorized access attempts

metadata.detection_notes: Assess whether continuous monitoring systems (CCTV, motion sensors, alarm systems, security personnel) are deployed and actively monitored. Absence of surveillance systems, unmonitored cameras, or lack of 24/7 monitoring indicates this deficiency. Note: A.7.4 is new in ISO 27001:2022.

signals.name: No Physical Security Perimeters
signals.description: Security perimeters are not defined and used to protect areas containing information and assets.
signals.applicability: Organizations with physical facilities that contain sensitive information or information processing equipment

metadata.detection_notes: Review facility documentation for defined security perimeters, physical barriers (walls, fences, gates), and documented access control zones. Absence of clearly defined perimeter boundaries or physical barriers indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Physical and Environmental Threat Protection
signals.canonical_name: No Physical and Environmental Threat Protection
signals.description: Protection against physical and environmental threats is not designed and implemented.
signals.applicability: Organizations requiring protection of information processing facilities from natural disasters, environmental hazards, and deliberate attacks

metadata.detection_notes: Review protection measures against natural disasters (fire, flood, earthquake), environmental threats (temperature, humidity), and malicious attacks. Absence of fire suppression, climate control, flood protection, or structural hardening indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Supporting Utilities Protection
signals.description: Information processing facilities are not protected from power failures and utility disruptions.
signals.applicability: Organizations with information processing facilities dependent on supporting utilities such as power, telecommunications, water, and HVAC systems

metadata.detection_notes: Assess protection measures for critical utilities including UPS systems, backup generators, redundant telecommunications, and HVAC systems. Absence of redundancy, backup power, or utility monitoring indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Information Access Restriction
signals.description: Access to information and application system functions is not restricted according to access control policy.
signals.applicability: Applies to organizations that do not enforce access restrictions to information and application functions based on defined access control policies, including lack of role-based access control (RBAC), attribute-based access control (ABAC), or need-to-know principles.

metadata.detection_notes: Review access control policies, implemented access controls in applications and systems, permission matrices, role definitions, access provisioning workflows, and enforcement mechanisms for least privilege and need-to-know.

signals.name: Missing Application Security Requirements
signals.description: Information security requirements are not identified, specified, and approved for application development. This signal indicates that applications are developed without documented security requirements, security acceptance criteria, or security specifications for authentication, authorization, data protection, and secure functionality.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all application development projects including web applications, mobile applications, desktop applications, APIs, microservices, cloud applications, and third-party application integrations. Includes both new development and modification of existing applications.

metadata.detection_notes: Commonly detected through review of requirements documentation, functional specifications, security requirements catalogs, acceptance criteria, user stories, and project approval processes. May also be identified through analysis of application development backlogs and security feature tracking.

signals.name: Unprotected Information Systems During Audit Testing
signals.canonical_name: Unprotected Information Systems During Audit Testing
signals.description: Audit tests and activities involving assessment of operational systems are not planned and controlled. This signal indicates that security audits, penetration testing, vulnerability assessments, or compliance testing activities are performed without proper planning, authorization, scope definition, or safeguards to prevent service disruption or data loss.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all audit and assessment activities including internal audits, external audits, penetration testing, vulnerability scanning, compliance assessments, security reviews, and system testing that involves operational production systems or sensitive data.
